Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Headache for 3 days, worsening, mainly around right eye, but also generalized.
- Nature of pain: Dull, sometimes becomes sharper; developed gradually; currently rated 8/10 severity.
- Course/progression: Started at work, increased over 3 days, worse on waking on the second day; ongoing and interfering with work concentration.
- Associated symptoms: Photophobia (light hurts eyes); occasional visual symptoms described as "shooting lights"; difficulty focusing; no vomiting, but feels nauseated; no neck pain or stiffness; no speech or limb weakness; no fever or rash.
- Previous episodes: Has had headaches before but less severe, typically responsive to ibuprofen; this episode is not responsive.
- Family history: Mother and sister have migraines.
- Past medical history: No other medical conditions reported. No history of migraines personally.
- Medications: Took ibuprofen (3 tablets/day for 2 days; exact dose/route/frequency not documented). No regular medications.
- Allergies: None known.
- Social history: Lives with 3 housemates. Works in IT (screen time; has had to reduce screen brightness due to symptoms); describes work as recently "a bit stressful" due to a new project. Social alcohol and tobacco use only. Wears glasses (no recent eye test).

Objective:
- No physical examination or vital signs documented.
- No investigations performed or results available.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Headache
   - Assessment: Likely migraine-type headache (first episode with features suggestive of migraine: right-sided, photophobia, possible visual aura, family history, not relieved by standard analgesia).
   - Differential diagnosis: Tension headache, cluster headache, sinusitis (not specifically discussed), secondary causes for headache (e.g. raised intracranial pressure, but no red flag symptoms elicited).
   - Investigations planned: None at this visit.
   - Treatment planned: 
     - Optimize ibuprofen dose (can take up to 2 tablets, three times daily per doctor).
     - Offer prescription for naproxen (dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Option to add paracetamol or codeine for additional pain control (dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Keep a headache diary to track triggers and frequency.
   - Safety net advice: Return urgently if headache worsens, vision changes, limb weakness, or other concerning symptoms develop.

2. Migraine Prophylaxis (Future consideration)
   - Assessment: Consider prophylactic medication if headaches become more frequent.
   - Treatment planned: To be discussed at follow-up if indicated.

3. Eye Care
   - Assessment: Visual symptoms reported; wears glasses; no recent eye exam.
   - Treatment planned: Advised to consider a repeat eye test if eye strain continues.

4. Follow-up
   - Treatment planned: Return in 1-2 weeks for reassessment. Return sooner if symptoms worsen or new neurological signs develop.

Quality checks:
●	Missing elements: No documentation of vital signs, neurological or fundoscopy examination, or medication reconciliation details beyond those discussed. 
●	Internal conflicts: Patient initially answers "yeah" to neck pain/stiffness, then says "no" (conflict noted).
●	Transcript quality: Clear overall; some minor filler and repetition, but clinically relevant information was extractable. No major inaudible sections.
